Messages.Author: Daniel Hoffman
Messages.Body:
>The blood doll isn't much good without giving your minions
>blood to draw off of. 1 HG per Blood Doll is +1 income.

>This card gives you another source to refill your vampires.
A source inferior to 5th trad, voter capivation, taste of vitae and old
fashioned hunting. Not to mention the rack and feeding razor and the Discotek
and restoration.

If you are looking to gain pool over time then use a Short Term or Protracted
investment, better yet use Ascendance and get your 1 pool immediately instead
of wasting blood dolls and 3 turns.

>I still wouldn't classify it as wallpaper.

Nothing is REALLY wallpaper except Concealed Weapon and Chainsaw without house
rules. Cards which have no realistic use are so called "worthless" or
"wallpaper". If you have 3+ Giovanni and it isn't destroyed is just too many
ifs to be worthwhile. People will destroy it if you have enough Giovanni to
make it worthwhile.

Ascendance is the biggest waste of a master card action known to man.
Protracted Investment probably makes number two. Better ways to get
pool are not limited to:

5th Trad. + Minion Tap (add Golconda and Soul Gem to taste)

Parity Shift

Anathema

Sacrificial Lamb

*Certainly* Blood Doll + HG, Rack, Navar McClaren hunting. It keeps on

versatility to keep blood on your vampires as needed, *or* feed you.
It's true I include it in fewer and fewer decks, but it still beats the
crap out of Ascendance.

Messages.Author: The Corrupter
Messages.Body:
In article <4e8hvb$j...@texas.nwlink.com>, "T.J. Hull" <t...@nwlink.com> wrote:

> Ascendance is the biggest waste of a master card action known to man.
> Protracted Investment probably makes number two. Better ways to get
> pool are not limited to:

Ascendence has the result of being able to be used immediately. In a
precarious position where you cannot afford to lose the blood from a
blood doll, can't afford the Investment, etc., Ascendence is useful.

Protracted Investment has less of a percentage payback then Short Term,
but in a deck with fewer masters, a Protracted investment is less card
intensive. Certainly two short term is better than one protracted
investment in terms of blood gain, but the protracted takes seven turns
to finish up, while the Short Term takes eight. In terms of a single card:

Card Blood Gain Time Spent
Ascendence 1 1
Short Term 2 4
Protracted 3 7

This seems reasonable.

> 5th Trad. + Minion Tap (add Golconda and Soul Gem to taste)

You must minion tap first, and your 5th tradition could be blocked. It
takes an action to use 5th Tradition. Golconda Loses a Vampire, and the
Soul Gem is not a guaranteer of a new vampires.

> Parity Shift

A vote that needs to be passed, and can only be called if you are losing
to another methuselah.

> Anathema

Another vote. Requires combat with another minion that you are not
necesarrily going to win. Other methuselahs may get the benefit instead
of you.

> Sacrificial Lamb

Can be blocked. Blood is gained, not pool.

> Edge

Easily stolen.

> *Certainly* Blood Doll + HG, Rack, Navar McClaren hunting. It keeps on
> giving and frees you up to do other stuff. Blood Doll has the
> versatility to keep blood on your vampires as needed, *or* feed you.
> It's true I include it in fewer and fewer decks, but it still beats the
> crap out of Ascendance.

Ascendence may be less useful in a broad sense then some of the other
examples above, but it is by no means a bad card. Its practical use is
more limited comparatively.
